name: Bitter-eggplant soup
summary: Êđê soup of bitter eggplant. One account uses dried fish and rice-washing water. Another uses beef offal. Both stay. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Bao Dak Lak calls canh cà đắng an Êđê specialty of Dak Lak.
howToEat: Bao Dak Lak on 26 Jul 2023: pound dried fish, fry it with onion and garlic, add water, and boil. Add bitter eggplant, forest greens, and herbs, especially culantro. Season, then thicken with rice-washing water. Eat it with white rice. The article calls the eggplant slightly harsh-bitter and the chili hot.

Bao Dak Lak on 24 Jun 2013 calls the standout version the soup with beef offal and wêc êmô, beef bung. Score the fruit in two or four, soak it in dilute brine, and add it when the pot boils. Then add the meat and the bung until soft. Forest greens can go in. Off the heat, crush the eggplant and add lá é and the scallion-like leaves and bulbs.

The Dak Lak provincial portal, 18 Feb 2019, also names fresh fish, dried shrimp, forest meat, and eggplant stewed with frog, and says chili, lá é, and those scallion-like leaves and bulbs are the three seasonings. It does not print a separate method for each. A price is Check on arrival.
where: Bao Dak Lak on 23 May 2023 places a meal of this soup under a stilt roof in Buon Don, Lak, or Buon Ma Thuot. A street number is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Canh ca dang — Ede bitter-eggplant soup
seoDescription: Ede bitter-eggplant soup. One account uses dried fish. Another uses beef offal and beef bung. A street number and a price are Check on arrival.
taste: Bao Dak Lak on 26 Jul 2023 calls the soup harsh-bitter from the eggplant and hot from the chili.
The 24 Jun 2013 article calls the beef-offal version deeply bitter, sweet from the offal, fragrant from the bung, and hot from the chili, with lá é and scallion.
